title: Lord of the Families Below
description: Lord of the Families Below in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 504, “Peace Be Unto This House”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord of the fam-i-lies be-low! To Thee our prayers we send; Do Thou from dan-ger and from woe This dwell-ing place de-fend.

lines: To Thee our prayers we send;
Do Thou from danger and from woe
Here let Thy peace, O Father, rest;
Our every joy in Thee more blest,
May our petitions when we meet,
Teach us, with hearts made one in love,
And give us, in Thy time, above,
A house not made with hands.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1866.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
